extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, patent owners, and counsel participating in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) and post-grant review (PGR) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the interim bifurcated process for institution decisions in PTAB IPR and PGR proceedings, including timing, briefing, evidence, Director review, Board panel responsibilities, conflicts, rehearing, and filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of bifurcated process
rubrics_metrics.description: The bifurcated process is available in IPRs and PGRs in which the patent owner files a preliminary response, or the deadline for patent owner to file a preliminary response occurs, after March 26, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent owner filed a POPR or the POPR deadline occurred on or before March 26, 2025, the bifurcated process is not available and the Board panel proceeds as before (addressing discretionary and merits considerations together) and will not consider new Process Memorandum factors or rehearing based on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for patent owner discretionary denial brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file a brief explaining any applicable bases for discretionary denial of institution within two months of the date on which the PTAB enters a Notice of Filing Date Accorded to a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may file their briefs early but may not stipulate to later due dates that would interfere with statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for petitioner opposition to discretionary denial brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner may file an opposition brief no later than 1 month after the due date for the patent owner discretionary denial brief (i.e., on the due date for the patent owner preliminary response (POPR)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave to file further briefing may be permitted by the Director for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension notice when brief due imminently to Process Memorandum
rubrics_metrics.description: If the time for filing a discretionary denial brief has not yet elapsed but will elapse in 1 month or less after issuance of the Process Memorandum, the Board will issue a notice extending the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that event, the patent owner may file a discretionary denial brief within 1 month of the date of the notice, and the petitioner may file an opposition no later than 1 month after the patent owner brief due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing when discretionary brief time elapsed but POPR deadline not passed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the time for filing a discretionary denial brief has elapsed, but the deadline for filing a POPR has not yet passed, the patent owner may file a discretionary denial brief within 1 month of the date of the Process Memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner may file an opposition to the discretionary denial brief no later than 1 month after the due date for the patent owner brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: No party stipulations to extend statutory deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure statutory deadlines are met, the parties may not stipulate to later due dates for filing the discretionary considerations briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may, however, file its discretionary denial brief or an opposition prior to the due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early filing does not change downstream timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner files its discretionary denial brief early, the timing for a petitioner’s opposition and the Director’s decision does not change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner opposition will still be due within 1 month of the due date for the patent owner brief (i.e., on the POPR due date) and the Director’s decision will not issue until after a patent owner files its POPR or the deadline for filing the POPR has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director procedures when patent owner files timely discretionary brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will receive each petition, discretionary denial brief, opposition brief, and POPR, as well as any evidence the parties have made of record, and will determine, in consultation with at least three senior PTAB judges separate from merits judges, whether discretionary denial is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may consult other USPTO personnel as needed (avoiding conflicts). When parties present arguments regarding the strength of the merits, the Director will consult USPTO personnel with relevant technical expertise. Absent good cause, the Director will issue a decision on discretionary considerations within 1 month of the due date of the last relevant paper filed and will explain why discretionary denial was exercised or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decisions issued only if patent owner files discretionary brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner chooses not to file a discretionary denial brief, the Director will not issue a decision on discretionary considerations; the Office will enter a notice indicating the case is before a Board panel to consider non-discretionary issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board panel will issue a decision on institution addressing merits and non-discretionary considerations and ordinarily will not address discretionary considerations except in limited situations involving insufficient challenges (see Chevron and Deeper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretion is not limited to parties' arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has broad authority and is not limited to the arguments the parties raise in their briefs when determining whether to exercise discretion to institute an IPR or PGR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may consider additional facts and circumstances to maintain consistency with prior discretionary decisions, where Office operations reveal relevant facts, or where record or public-domain facts are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of responsibility for institution decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the bifurcated process, the Director retains authority over institution decisions but delegates responsibilities depending on whether a patent owner files a discretionary denial brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent owner timely files a brief, the Director retains responsibility for discretionary denial. If the Director determines discretionary denial is not appropriate, responsibility for preparing the institution decision on merits and other non-discretionary issues is delegated to a Board panel (typically 2 months to issue the decision). If no patent owner brief is filed, responsibility passes to a Board panel the day after the due date for the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of discretionary vs non-discretionary (merits) considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Merits’ considerations concern whether there is a reasonable likelihood a petitioner would prevail on at least one challenged claim in IPR, or whether it is more likely than not for PGR, among other statutory questions; non-discretionary considerations include statutes (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §§ 311, 312, 315(a),(b),(e), 322, 325(a),(e)) and related requirements such as claim construction and meeting 37 C.F.R. § 42.104(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Process Memorandum includes a non-exhaustive list of discretionary issues; parties are encouraged to address any fact or circumstance bearing on the Director’s discretion, including reasons not discussed in precedent. Discretionary considerations can include whether a petition presents a sufficient number of grounds that meet the reasonable likelihood standard (see Chevron and Deeper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits arguments in discretionary briefs not later considered by Board panel
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines discretionary denial is not appropriate, the Board panel will not consider papers filed relating to discretionary considerations; parties must make merits arguments in the petition, POPR, and any authorized reply or sur-reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will consider merits in discretionary review if the parties ask; parties should not repeat merits arguments verbatim in discretionary briefing but may briefly explain why merits are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board panels not bound by Director’s merit findings in discretionary decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board panel is not bound by merit findings or conclusions in a discretionary consideration decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the panel's findings differ, it must explain why and cite the parties' evidence of record as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of Sotera or Sand stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner should file a Sotera or Sand stipulation as soon as practicable so the patent owner may address the stipulation in its discretionary denial brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will consider whether the stipulation materially reduces overlap between proceedings. In cases relying on corresponding system art in co-pending proceedings or multiple invalidity theories, a stipulation may not meaningfully increase efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder motions handled consistent with timing and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for joinder are handled the same with respect to processes and timing; the bifurcated process availability depends on POPR filing/deadline relative to March 26, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision on joinder and joining a party to an instituted proceeding is made by a Board merits panel. Parties disagreeing may file a request for Director Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to request permission to file reply to petitioner’s opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner who wants to request a reply should send an email request, with a copy to counsel for all parties, to Director_Discretionary_Decision@USPTO.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The email should be timely and copied to all counsel of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board panel decides good cause for replies to POPR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board panel determines whether good cause exists for a petitioner to file a reply to a POPR or for a patent owner to file a sur-reply to such a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of patent owner testimonial evidence at the preliminary stage may warrant granting the petitioner a reply. A request to file a reply must make a showing of good cause; scope and whether to allow the reply rests with the Board panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural motions not related to discretionary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro hac vice motions and other procedural motions not related to discretionary considerations will be decided by the Board panel regardless of when filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate resolution, PTAB will assign a Board panel to the case before the Director issues a decision on discretionary considerations; that panel will decide all procedural motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limits for discretionary consideration briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner’s discretionary denial brief is limited to 14,000 words and a petitioner’s opposition brief is limited to 14,000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should adhere to these word limits when preparing discretionary briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of issues to raise in discretionary briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to address any fact or circumstance they believe bears on whether the Office should or should not institute trial, including reasons not discussed in current Board precedent or the Process Memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list in the Process Memorandum is non-exhaustive; parties should include any relevant facts or operational considerations that bear on Director’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reliance on expert testimony in petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive reliance on expert testimony and/or reasonable disputes between experts on dispositive issues may suggest the questions are better resolved in an Article III court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute and case law require petitions be based on prior art patents and printed publications. Experts should provide focused testimony (context or explanation of terms of art). Failure to provide focused expert testimony may weigh against institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a discretionary denial brief to raise discretionary issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If the bifurcated process is available, a patent owner must raise discretionary denial issues in a discretionary denial brief; absent extraordinary circumstances, the Director and the Board panel will not consider discretionary arguments raised in a POPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no discretionary denial brief is filed, the Board panel will address merits and other non-discretionary considerations raised in petition, POPR, and any authorized replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: If discretionary brief due after POPR, still file separate discretionary brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner’s discretionary denial brief is due after the due date of the POPR (due to an extension or Process Memorandum 1-month rule), the patent owner must file a discretionary denial brief to have discretionary issues considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent extraordinary circumstances, a Board panel will not address discretionary considerations presented in a POPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition should not address discretionary issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition should not address discretionary issues; a petitioner should raise any discretionary issues in its opposition to a patent owner’s discretionary denial brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner opposition should include issues relating to 35 U.S.C. § 325(d), parallel proceedings, parallel petitions, serial petitions, and any other matters bearing on the Director's discretion to institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on merits or claim construction arguments in discretionary briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should not treat a discretionary denial brief or opposition as an additional opportunity for merits briefing, though a patent owner may direct attention to an anticipated POPR and evidence for a discussion of the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may refer to arguments made in the petition and cite record evidence. The Director will consider the petition and POPR merits arguments when relevant to discretion. Parties’ discretionary briefing may also address claim construction if relevant to discretionary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence allowed with discretionary briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may introduce evidence relevant to the discretionary issues raised in their briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will consider the petition, the POPR, and the evidence cited therein in determining whether discretionary denial is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing and Director Review procedures for discretionary vs merits issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request rehearing by a Board panel only if the request raises merits and other non-discretionary issues; a party may request rehearing by the Director if the request only raises discretionary considerations. To raise both types, file a request for Director Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director exercises discretion to deny institution, a party may file a request for rehearing or Director Review within 30 days of the Director’s decision. If the Director determines discretionary denial is not appropriate, file a single request for rehearing or Director Review after the Board panel issues its decision. Incorrectly filed rehearing requests will be treated as Director Review and require refiling and fee payment under 37 C.F.R. § 42.75(c) and § 42.15(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing of institution decisions raising only merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a request for rehearing of a decision on institution that raises issues regarding merits or other non-discretionary considerations but does not raise discretionary considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a party may file either a request for rehearing by the Board panel or a request for Director Review (but not both).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changed circumstances after Director decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If circumstances change after the Director issues a decision on discretionary considerations (e.g., a trial date changes), a party may raise that fact in a request for rehearing or a request for Director Review filed within the applicable time period in exceptional cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changed circumstances should be raised promptly and only in exceptional situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director, a consulting PTAB member, or any other USPTO employee has a conflict of interest, they shall recuse themselves from the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO follows Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch at 5 C.F.R. Part 2635 and consults with the Department of Commerce Ethics Law and Programs Office as needed. Conflicts may include involvement in examination or prosecution of the underlying patent or a related patent. PTAB judges consulting with the Director will additionally follow conflict guidance in SOP 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing PO Discretionary Denial Brief in P-TACTS
rubrics_metrics.description: After the PTAB issues a Notice of Filing Date Accorded and accepts a patent owner's Mandatory Notice, the new paper type 'PO Discretionary Denial Brief' will be available in P-TACTS and can be filed via the My Docket > +Add > File Other Document workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: log into P-TACTS; open case viewer; select +Add/File Other Document; choose 'PO Discretionary Denial Brief'; fill required fields marked by a red asterisk; select 'PO Discretionary Denial Brief'; click 'Add to List' then 'Submit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing PET Opposition to Discretionary Denial Brief in P-TACTS
rubrics_metrics.description: After a patent owner files its discretionary denial brief, the 'PET Opposition to Discretionary Denial Brief' paper type will be available in P-TACTS and can be filed using the File Other Document modal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: log into P-TACTS; open case viewer; select +Add/File Other Document; choose 'PET Opposition to Discretionary Denial Brief'; fill required fields; select the paper type; click 'Add to List' then 'Submit.'
